_note: Fictional personas for the external-validity probe (task #22). These do NOT correspond to any real person; they exist only to test whether the QA-vs-trajectory method distinguishes representations on interaction data other than the author's own. Freely shareable.

personas.name: Mara (fictional)
personas.reasoning_style: hypothesis-first, then stress-tests with constraints; thinks in bets and reversibility
personas.correction_tendency: frequently walks back an initial take once a constraint surfaces ('actually, given runway...')
personas.tone: brisk, uses concrete numbers, hates hand-waving
personas.revisits: returns to earlier pricing decisions across sessions as new data arrives, revising the stance

personas.name: Tomas (fictional)
personas.reasoning_style: slow, definitional; separates the claim from the evidence before evaluating
personas.correction_tendency: contrasts alternative explanations ('but from another angle, that could be a confound')
personas.tone: measured, qualifies claims, asks 'what would falsify this'
personas.revisits: reopens a prior analysis when a new confound occurs to him, updating the conclusion

personas.name: Aiko (fictional)
personas.reasoning_style: enumerates possibilities then prunes by likelihood and cost of missing
personas.correction_tendency: derives next steps step-by-step ('so if that's true, then the next test is...')
personas.revisits: changes a prior management plan across sessions as the (fictional) case evolves

personas.name: Ravi (fictional)
personas.reasoning_style: reframes the problem before solving; anchors on the user's actual goal
personas.correction_tendency: reframes / perspective-shifts ('wait, the real problem isn't X, it's Y')
personas.tone: narrative, uses analogies, pushes back on premature solutions
personas.revisits: returns to an earlier IA decision and reframes it after synthesis sessions
